statements.status_notes: CVE-2024-38827 affects Spring Framework's authorization rules when using locale-dependent String.toLowerCase() and String.toUpperCase(). The fix requires Spring Framework 6.1.14, a major version jump from the current 5.3.39. Upgrading to Spring 6.x would require Java 17 baseline and significant API changes incompatible with Data Prepper's current architecture. The vulnerability requires an application to use Spring Security with locale-sensitive authorization rules. Data Prepper does not use Spring Security; authentication is handled via HTTP Basic in the management API configuration. Investigation ongoing for a backport or alternative mitigation.

CVE-2024-38820 affects Spring Framework's DataBinder disallowedFields validation when using locale-dependent String.toLowerCase(). The fix requires Spring Framework 6.1.14, a major version jump from the current 5.3.39. Upgrading to Spring 6.x would require Java 17 baseline and significant API changes incompatible with Data Prepper's current architecture. The vulnerability requires an application to rely on disallowedFields patterns with locale-sensitive characters for security boundaries. Data Prepper uses Spring primarily for dependency injection and does not expose DataBinder-based form binding to untrusted input. Investigation ongoing for a backport or alternative mitigation.

Data Prepper 2.16.0 ships Spring Framework 5.3.39. This bypasses the CVE-2024-38820 fix; its only open-source fix is Spring 6.1.20/6.2.7, a major-version upgrade not yet adopted, and the 5.3.x backport is Enterprise Support only, absent from Maven Central. Monitoring for an adoptable fix.

CVE-2024-38827 is a Spring Security advisory (spring-security-core AuthorizationManager case-sensitivity). Data Prepper ships Spring Framework 5.3.39 but does not depend on Spring Security, so the vulnerable component is not present in the image.
